Nothing asked whether the file was a manifest before JSON.parse: prepare_velocity_intake_release.js threw and Velocity Content Release went red (run 34977580334); agent-artifact-continuity read it as {} and hard-failed Validate Repo (run 34977580273) on 'vertical mismatch: undefined'; agent-artifact-stranding skipped it in silence; count_unabsorbed_agent_runs.mjs did not count it, so no catch-up dispatch would ever retry it. 2026-07-20 personal-injury was the same writer defect (byte-corrupted keys, unresolved local-fetch pointers) and was repaired by hand three days later. This validator exercises the write-time guard (writeJsonVerified: serialize, write to a temp file, read it back, parse, rename - a failed write leaves no file and the previous file intact), checks both report_fixes JSON writers route through it, exercises the quarantine path on the real 2026-09-15 bytes and the 2026-07-20 pointer shape, classifies every landed drop (defective inside the absorption window is a NAMED pending quarantine; past it a hard failure naming the file and defects), and parses every repo-written JSON under data/report_fixes. 2026-09-30 trt.csv was the third writer defect: 427 em dashes and arrows arrived double-encoded (UTF-8 read as Latin-1 and encoded again) beside correctly encoded characters, intake copied them into every derived ledger and trt/index.html, and search-quality-basics blocked every release on trt/index.html:mojibake. This validator now proves that exact shape reads back as the intended text through readArtifactText (the delivered bytes untouched), that mojibake the repair cannot decode is refused at intake as a named double_encoded_utf8_unrepairable defect, that the three raw-artifact readers route through the repairing reader, and that release and intake share one mojibake definition.

STRONG_WARNING.title: Citation-occupancy control separation and open-bucket integrity
STRONG_WARNING.risk_prevented: Makes the occupancy probe's own control pair binding. FAILS the run when the pair INVERTS - the query known to be CLOSED measuring more open than the one known to be OPEN, which is what happened (1.00 against 0.50) while the check was only a printed note and five pages were queued for publication off the numbers it did not stop. Re-classifies every recorded citation host with the shared classifier and FAILS if any unrecognised host is counted as open, or if a recorded open/unclassifiable count does not match what the hosts derive. FAILS if a citation_occupancy number is published while the controls do not separate, or withheld while they do. Requires the unclassifiable slot count on every run. Hard-fails if it examines zero probes, zero cited hosts or zero controls. 2026-10-07: also FAILS when the two arms overlap (a control query measured again under any other role, a duplicate query, two rows claiming one control role, or both controls the same query), when summary.control_separation_ok disagrees with the separation recomputed from the control probes, and when data/authority_scale/query_atlas.json carries a measured citation_occupancy basis while the pair does not separate. A pair that does not separate is a NAMED STOP printed on every run, not a failure: the number is withheld and nothing downstream reads it.

Tier 7.title: No tracked file carries a git conflict marker
Tier 7.risk_prevented: A tracked file could reach main carrying git conflict markers. On 2026-09-09 PRs #99, #100 and #101 were each rebased onto a main that had moved and the conflicts - all in regenerable validation receipts - were resolved with directory pathspecs (git checkout --theirs -- artifacts), which silently leaves any file git had already written markers into exactly as it found it. 28 receipts reached main corrupted, 828 marker lines in validation-summary-release.json alone. Nothing caught it: JSON with a conflict marker does not parse, so every reader fell into a catch and treated the file as ABSENT rather than corrupt - publish_gate_decision.mjs could not read the release summary at all. A corrupt receipt is worse than a missing one because it looks present. This scans every tracked text file for a marker at the start of a line.

Tier 3.title: Primary-source and claim registry integrity, including retired authority URLs
Tier 3.risk_prevented: Regulated or numeric pages could ship with missing, dangling, or malformed provenance records. ALSO PINS RETIRED AUTHORITY URLS (16 Oct 2026). Every state page cites a licensing board or a federal programme page by URL, and those publishers move pages without redirecting. Danielle's site-audit crawl of theindustryguides.com found nine such links serving 404 from live guide pages: the Montana, Iowa, South Dakota, Connecticut and Tennessee psychology boards, the Tennessee medical board, the CMS state-based exchange list, and the Georgia Medicaid dental fee schedule, whose quarterly PDF filename carries a publication timestamp GAMMIS rotates so a direct link rots within three months. A claim sourced to a dead URL is the root of a false public claim, which is this validator's own hard_fail_basis, so the pin lives here rather than as a forty-first blocker. scripts/lib/retired_authority_urls.js holds the retired/live pairs and the evidence for each; this validator calls it. It fails when a retired URL reappears in the evidence or page-family source files or in any rendered HTML, AND when a replacement URL is absent from the source files, which is what 'fixed to nothing' looks like. Deliberately offline: a live crawl in CI would go red on a publisher bot-blocking us (ftc.gov 404s its own root to this egress) or on a hosting outage (medicaid.ms.gov was serving a temporary-site notice on 2026-10-16); both were investigated on 16 Oct and left unpinned because neither was a defect on our side.
